headline: Mazzulla Wins Coach Of The Year But Sox Fall Again At Fenway
morning_brew: Another frustrating night at Fenway Park as the Red Sox fell seven to six against the Atlanta Braves. Ranger Suarez had a rough outing on the mound, giving up five earned runs on six hits in five innings to pick up the loss. The bats tried to make a game of it, putting up nine hits and rallying for two runs in the ninth inning, but the mountain was just too high to climb. This team is now twenty-two and thirty-one, and the pitching lapses are making it incredibly hard to string wins together.

Even though the Celtics had a highly disappointing postseason, some great news came out of the Garden on Tuesday night. Joe Mazzulla was officially named the NBA Coach of the Year, beating out the other finalists for the award. He guided the team to fifty-six wins during the regular season, and while the first-round exit still stings, this is a well-deserved honor for the head coach. Now the pressure is on the front office to make the right moves this offseason so Joe Mazzulla has the roster he needs to make another deep run.

Over on the ice, the Bruins are facing their own crucial offseason after a first-round exit. The front office needs to be aggressive in free agency and the draft to build a more consistent roster around David Pastrnak. Finding some extra scoring depth has to be the top priority because relying too heavily on a few guys is not a recipe for postseason success. It is going to be a busy summer in Boston, and both winter teams have a lot of questions to answer before training camp rolls around.

news_digest.headline: Celtics' Joe Mazzulla named 2025-26 NBA Coach of the Year
news_digest.dans_take: A great individual honor for Joe, but the ultimate goal remains bringing postseason success back to Boston.
